::: {#rem-quantifier-notation}
#### Reading and writing quantifiers

English has many phrasings of each quantifier:

- $\forall$: "for all", "for every", "for each", "for any", "every", "all".
- $\exists$: "there exists", "there is", "for some", "some", "at least one".

Books also differ in punctuation:
$\forall x \in S, P(x)$ is also written
$\forall x \in S : P(x)$, $(\forall x \in S)\, P(x)$, or $\forall x \in S .\, P(x)$.
When the domain is clear, it is often left out, as in $\forall x, P(x)$.

:::
